'''''Polypodium cambricum''''', the '''southern polypody''',<ref>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17}}</ref> '''limestone polypody''',<ref>{{cite journal|author=Hackney, P.|title=''Polypodium australe'' Fee in the North of Ireland|journal=The Irish Naturalists' Journal|year=1977|volume=19|issue=4|pages=104–107|jstor=25538081}}</ref> or '''Welsh polypody''', is a [[species]] of [[fern]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Polypodiaceae, [[native plant|native]] to southern and western Europe where it grows on shady rocks, near the coasts of the [[Mediterranean Basin]] and in the mountains of [[Atlantic Europe]]. It is a spreading, terrestrial, [[deciduous]] fern growing to {{convert|60|cm}} tall, with pinnate fronds. The [[sorus|sori]] are yellow in winter.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref>

==Description==
Perennial. [[Rhizome]] elongate, often above ground, densely covered with rusty scales. Fronds distich, {{convert|5|–|30|cm}}, glabrous, deltoid in outline; petiole yellowish green, shorter than the pinnatipartite limb. Segments 5-28 on each side; margin dentate, marked with a strong midrib. Sori round, {{convert|2|–|4|mm}} in diameter, orange-yellow, arranged on each side of the midrib of segments. The fruits bloom from February to July.
==Name==
This species has been widely known by the more apt name ''P. australe'' {{small|Fée}}. However, since Linnaeus did mention the species, albeit in the aberrant ''cambricum''-form, that name must have priority.{{citation needed|date=December 2023}}

==Etymology==
''Polypodium'' is derived from the Greek ''Polus'', many, and ''podion'', small foot, since the rhizome bears numerous roots. 
The [[Botanical name#Binary name|specific epithet]] ''cambricum'' means "Welsh",<ref>{{cite book|author=Harrison, Lorraine|title=RHS Latin for gardeners|year=2012|publisher=Mitchell Beazley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=9781845337315|pages=224}}</ref> from the Latinized form of ''[[Cambria|Cymru]]'', the Welsh name for Wales. 

''Australe'' comes from the Latin {{Lang|la|auter}}, the wind of the south, for in [[Europe]], this species grows largely in the [[Mediterranean Basin]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Roberts, R. H.|author2=Synnott, D. M.|title=Polypodium australe Fee in Scotland and North East Ireland|journal=Watsonia|volume=9|pages=39–41|year=1972|url=http://archive.bsbi.org.uk/Wats9p39.pdf}}</ref>

*'Grandiceps Fox' (Cristatum Group)<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/108486/Polypodium-cambricum-(Cristatum-Group)-Grandiceps-Fox/Details | title = ''Polypodium cambricum'' (Cristatum Group) 'Grandiceps Fox' | publisher = RHS | access-date = 18 January 2021}}</ref>
